issue: Grammatical, but pragmatically odd: flatly telling someone 'Anda manajer kami' to their face is not a sentence natives produce; superiors are addressed as Pak/Bu, not informed of their own role. Works better as third-person identification.

adalah where copula-drop is natural: no native says 'Dia adalah adik saya' across a table — adalah belongs in definitions/formal writing (cf. id-0028), not a personal kinship statement. Q1 register policy requires neutral conversational; the tip even admits adalah is optional yet the card models the stiff variant.

fix.grammar: In conversation just drop 'is': Dia adik saya. adalah sounds formal, like a definition.

issue: Gloss mismatch: English 'They come from Surabaya' reads as origin/hometown (berasal dari), but datang dari describes a movement event (arrived/traveled from). Fix the gloss to the motion reading.
English calque: 'Apakah Anda punya kamar kosong?' transplants 'Do you have a vacant room?' word-for-word. At a hotel desk natives ask availability with (masih) ada, not punya addressed to the clerk.

fix.english: Are there still any rooms available?

issue: Stiff for the situation: a late-night check-in like this is asked with plain rising intonation, not formal Apakah + belum; and the gloss 'Have you not slept yet?' is stilted English no one says. Intonation questions are already taught (id-0066), so the natural form fits the deck.

Gloss adds information not in the Indonesian: adik is gender-neutral 'younger sibling' (the deck's own gloss at id-0024/id-0060), but here it is rendered 'little brother'. Inconsistent and unfaithful.

fix.target: Adik sedang belajar untuk ujian besok.
fix.english: My younger sibling is studying for tomorrow's exam.
fix.grammar: untuk = for (purpose): belajar untuk ujian (study for the exam)

issue: Loose noun phrase: 'mulai kerja baru' uses bare kerja as the noun 'job'; standard conversational Indonesian says pekerjaan baru (kerja-as-noun leans colloquial, e.g. 'dapat kerjaan'). pekerjaan already appears elsewhere in the deck, so no new vocabulary.

fix.target: Dia akan mulai pekerjaan baru bulan depan.
fix.english: She will start a new job next month.
